citations.narrative:
The welded wire fencing containing the five emus is hanging loosely and bowed inward indicating a loss of tension.
Several fence posts are leaning significantly rather than standing upright. The horizontal wires show uneven spacing and
a wavy, distorted appearance. Fencing that is damaged or in disrepair can injure birds or allow them to escape. Housing
facilities for birds must be kept in good repair and protect the birds from injury. To be corrected by September 11, 2026.

Multiple primary enclosures require maintenance and repair:
• In the enclosure housing two dromedary camels the top horizontal gate fence rail is bent downward at the center
creating a noticeable dip. The connection where the diagonal support bar meets the top rail is broken and separated
leaving the brace loose and exposing a sharp edge. The gate frame also appears warped and due to the bent top rail it no
longer maintains its proper rectangular shape.
• The welded wire fencing containing the zebra is hanging loosely and bowed inward indicating a loss of tension. Several
fence posts are leaning significantly rather than standing upright. The horizontal wires show uneven spacing and a wavy,
distorted appearance. According to the caretaker the zebra frequently reaches over and pulls the fence down in an
attempt to access grass on the opposite side.
Fencing that is damaged or in disrepair can injure livestock or allow them to escape. Housing facilities shall be maintained
in good repair to protect the animals from injury and contain the animals. To be corrected by September 11, 2026.
This inspection and exit interview were conducted with facility representatives.
